title: Build a tiny word tokenizer
summary: A tokenizer turns text into pieces and IDs. WordLevel uses whole pieces from a supplied vocabulary. Whitespace splits this simple sentence into words.
introduction: A tokenizer turns text into pieces and IDs. WordLevel uses whole pieces from a supplied vocabulary. Whitespace splits this simple sentence into words. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain build a tiny word tokenizer
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A tokenizer turns text into pieces and IDs. WordLevel uses whole pieces from a supplied vocabulary. Whitespace splits this simple sentence into words.

blocks.code:
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
from tokenizers.models import WordLevel
from tokenizers.pre_tokenizers import Whitespace

tokenizer = Tokenizer(WordLevel({"[PAD]": 0, "[UNK]": 1, "moon": 2, "glows": 3}, unk_token="[UNK]"))
tokenizer.pre_tokenizer = Whitespace()
encoded = tokenizer.encode("moon glows")
print(encoded.tokens, encoded.ids)
blocks.title: Build a tiny word tokenizer

blocks.text: The output shows ['moon', 'glows'] and [2, 3]. The vocabulary assigns those IDs, and the pre-tokenizer separates the words before lookup.
